name: paywall
description: One-entitlement monetization: monthly/annual subscriptions + lifetime unlock via RevenueCat, feature gates that resolve OPEN when unconfigured (ship-dark safety), and a compliant custom paywall sheet. The SDK is confined to client.ts; everything else is SDK-free and testable.

requires.why: Only for identity: pass the backend user id to <MonetizationProvider appUserId={...}> so signed-out purchases alias to the account on sign-in (Purchases.logIn). Without accounts, pass null; anonymous purchases and Restore still work.
The paywall example tracks the purchase funnel (Paywall Viewed, Purchase Started/Completed/Failed, Purchases Restored). Without analytics, strip the track() calls from the app-owned PaywallSheet.

notes: 10.2.1 is the hard floor on RN 0.79+ (NativeEventEmitter crash fix); the blueprint pins ^10.4.2.
Do NOT add react-native-purchases-ui: it is exact-version-locked to the core SDK, has a rougher new-architecture history, and this module ships a custom paywall instead.
No config plugin exists or is needed (bare or prebuild).
Real purchases need a development build; Expo Go only offers mock Preview data.

BOTH SDKs are required LAZILY inside their one-door files (client.ts, paywall-ui.ts) — a static import crashes every binary built before the native modules existed. Never convert to static imports; keep the two packages version-locked to each other.

EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_IOS_KEY.prompt: RevenueCat iOS public SDK key (Project > API keys, appl_...). Leave blank to ship dark:
EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_IOS_KEY.description: Publishable client key, safe to bundle. Empty = monetization off for the build: no paid UI renders and every feature gate resolves open.

EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_ANDROID_KEY.prompt: RevenueCat Android public SDK key (goog_...). Leave blank to ship dark:
EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_ANDROID_KEY.description: Publishable client key, safe to bundle. Same ship-dark behavior as iOS.

notes: Bare apps: Xcode > target > Signing & Capabilities > add In-App Purchase.
Autolinking handles the pod; just run pod install.
Prefer launchMode standard/singleTop for the main activity; if the app relies on singleTask for deep links, keep it but verify the sandbox purchase flow completes before changing anything.

revenuecat: Create project; add App Store + Play Store apps with the app's bundle id / package.
Upload the App Store Connect In-App Purchase Key (StoreKit 2 records NO transactions without it).
Entitlements: create one (default id 'plus'); attach every product to it.
Mark any lifetime product NON-consumable (a consumable one-time product gets consumed on SDK 10+ and cannot be restored).
appstoreconnect: Paid Applications agreement + banking + tax must be Active or getOfferings() returns empty.
Subscription group + auto-renewing products; lifetime as Non-Consumable.
The FIRST IAP must be submitted attached to an app version.
playconsole: Subscriptions + in-app product; upload a BILLING-permission build to a closed track; add license testers and open the tester opt-in URL.

wrapRoot.placementNote: Needs appUserId. With the accounts module: a small bridge component inside <AccountsProvider> reads useAccounts().user and passes user?.id ?? null. Without accounts: <MonetizationProvider appUserId={null}>.

governance.policy: Content is never paywalled; no claw-backs; growth loops and the account are never gated; every gated feature gets a key + copy in gates.ts in the same change; no SDK import outside client.ts; prices only from the store.

agentInstructions.note: Append (never overwrite); fenced with BEGIN/END markers for in-place re-sync.

verify: npx tsc --noEmit passes in the app
App unit tests cover: unconfigured state resolves every gate open; configured-without-entitlement locks; package mapping keeps store price strings verbatim
pod install succeeds and RNPurchases appears in Podfile.lock
grep confirms react-native-purchases is imported ONLY in lib/monetization/client.ts
A keyless build shows no paid UI anywhere (ship-dark check)
With sandbox keys: purchase, restore, kill-app-offline persistence, and signed-out-purchase-then-sign-in merge all verified on device (see the app's monetization-setup-remaining doc)
